hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Laptop GPU, 4096 MiB VRAM

results.notes: Full 32,224-chunk index already built and in production use. Numbers match the Phase P1 section-aware vector-mode benchmark exactly.

Loads fine once SentenceTransformerEmbedder was patched to force use_safetensors=True (the installed torch 2.5.1 refuses a pickle-based .bin checkpoint per CVE-2025-32434; this fix is now shipped in finqa_v2/retrieval/embed.py and applies to every model, not just bge-m3). Throughput degrades sharply over the run (9.8/s -> 1.9/s in the first 2000/32224 chunks, likely thermal throttling -- GPU held at 86-88C -- and/or memory-pressure overhead near this GPU's 4GB ceiling). Extrapolated full-corpus time exceeds 4 hours. Killed before completion; no index was built. Fails the roadmap's resource/latency acceptance bar regardless of retrieval quality.

results.status: rejected -- impractical on this hardware (also needed a compatibility patch to load at all)
results.load_time_issue: First attempt crashed on load: AttributeError: 'XLMRobertaLoRA' object has no attribute 'all_tied_weights_keys'. Jina's trust_remote_code custom modeling classes (cached from https://huggingface.co/jinaai/xlm-roberta-flash-implementation) predate a transformers internal refactor and never set that attribute themselves; a newer transformers method reads it unconditionally. Worked around with an in-process monkeypatch (defaults the attribute to {} when a custom subclass didn't set it) for this evaluation only -- NOT applied to finqa_v2/retrieval/embed.py, since patching around a third-party remote-code/transformers version mismatch is not something to ship silently.
results.notes: Starts faster than bge-m3 (22/s vs 9.8/s) but degrades the same way -- 22/s -> 4.5/s in the first 2200/32224 chunks, extrapolated ETA 110+ min and still climbing. flash_attn is not installed (PyTorch-native attention fallback, slower). Killed before completion; no index was built. Fails the resource/latency bar, and the load-time incompatibility itself is a maintainability red flag independent of speed.

decision.rationale: Both candidate models were actually attempted (not assumed) on the real corpus and real hardware, per §7's rule. Both are rejected on resource/latency grounds alone -- neither finished embedding even 10% of the 32,224-chunk corpus in a reasonable time window, with throughput degrading further as each run progressed rather than stabilizing. This is a hardware-constrained verdict specific to this RTX 3050 4GB laptop GPU, not a claim that these models are worse in general; a stronger GPU (more VRAM, no thermal throttling) could change the outcome. Re-benchmark if the deployment target's hardware changes.
